definition: means a period from the inception of this Policy during which specified diseases / treatments are not covered. On completion of the Waiting Period, diseases / treatments shall be covered provided the Policy has been continuously renewed without any break
plain: A stretch of time at the start of a policy when certain conditions are not covered yet. It runs from the day the policy begins, not from the day you fall ill.
whyItMatters: Waiting periods are why insurance has to be bought before you need it rather than when you need it. They pass whether or not you hold a policy, so the cheapest year to start serving them is the earliest one. Buying young is mostly about getting these out of the way while you are healthy.
